implementationPlan.description: WRITE THE FAILING TEST FILE FIRST AND CAPTURE RED PROOF. Create moe-vscode/tests/plan-approval-client.test.cjs following the existing convention in tests/metrics-view.test.cjs exactly: `node:test` + `node:assert/strict`, read src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts off disk, compile it with `ts.transpileModule` (CommonJS / ES2020 / esModuleInterop) and run the output in a `vm` context so the tests execute PRODUCTION code rather than a copy of its logic. The context must stub the modules the client imports: a `vscode` shim whose `EventEmitter` records listeners and exposes `event`/`fire`/`dispose` and whose `window.createOutputChannel` returns an object with `appendLine`/`dispose`, plus inert `fs`, `path`, `net`, `child_process` and a `ws` default export exposing a constructor and the numeric `OPEN` constant. Build a helper that constructs the client, injects a fake socket by setting the private `ws` field and the private connection-state field to 'connected' with `readyState` equal to the stubbed OPEN, and records every string handed to `send`. Tests to write, each asserting the EXACT parsed JSON frame, not a substring: (A) `approveTask('task-1', 0)` sends payload `{ taskId: 'task-1', expectedPlanRevision: 0 }` — zero must survive, which kills a falsy-check mutant; (B) a normal value such as 7 and `Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER` both survive unchanged; (C) `approveTask('task-1')` sends payload `{ taskId: 'task-1' }` with the property genuinely ABSENT — assert with a key check, not an undefined comparison; (D) the same omitted-argument call while the cached state holds that task at a DIFFERENT revision still omits the key, proving the reviewed token is never inferred from current state; (E) explicit `undefined` behaves as omitted; (F) each malformed token — null, '3', true, 3.5, -1, Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1, NaN, Infinity — returns false, sends NOTHING at all (no legacy fallback frame), and fires an error event naming the APPROVE_TASK operation; (G) while disconnected, a valid approval still returns false and sends nothing, and a socket whose `send` throws still returns false and fires an error event, so no path reports false success; (H) an inbound ERROR frame in the modern shape (top-level operation/code/codeName plus context with taskId and both revisions) reaches the error event with operation, code, codeName and exactly those three context keys; (I) the same assertion for the legacy nested `payload.operation` shape; (J) an ERROR frame whose context also carries unrelated keys such as an internal field name, a reason string or a filesystem path promotes NONE of them, and an ERROR frame with no context at all yields no context property; (K) a TASK_UPDATED frame carrying planRevision leaves it readable on the cached task, and one WITHOUT the field leaves the property absent rather than coerced to zero. Realm-crossing Error. `throw new Error(...)` from the test realm is NOT `instanceof` the vm realm's Error, so the client silently took its `String(err)` branch and the message read 'Error: socket is gone'. The harness now exposes `vm.runInContext('Error', context)` and the test throws a vm-realm Error, exercising the real branch.

A vacuous assertion. `connectSocket(sendImpl)` originally replaced the recorder with the custom impl, so `assert.deepEqual(sent, [])` in the throwing-socket test could never fail. `send` now records the frame BEFORE delegating, and that test asserts the frame DID reach the socket carrying the token — proving the false came from the send, not from a local refusal.

Assertion style, chosen for mutation resistance and vm-realm safety: outbound frames are compared as EXACT parsed JSON objects (strings cross realms as primitives, so deepEqual is safe there); key absence is proven with `Object.keys(...)` and `hasOwnProperty`, never an `=== undefined` comparison that a serialized null would pass; error-event payloads are vm-realm objects so they are asserted field-by-field plus a sorted `Object.keys` set, per mem:gotcha-vscode-panel-strict-require-map's prototype trap.

implementationPlan.description: FORWARD THE REVIEWED TOKEN FROM THE CLIENT WITHOUT INVENTING ONE. In moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts change the method to `approveTask(taskId: string, expectedPlanRevision?: number): boolean`. When the argument is `undefined` send exactly the legacy payload `{ taskId }` with no extra property — this is the whole backwards-compatibility contract for the four unchanged callers. When it is supplied, validate it locally: accept only `typeof expectedPlanRevision === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger(expectedPlanRevision) && expectedPlanRevision >= 0`. `Number.isSafeInteger` is what rejects fractional, non-finite and out-of-range values; never use a numeric conversion here, because coercion is exactly the silent fallback this task exists to prevent. The error handling for a malformed token is: log it, fire the error event with `operation: 'APPROVE_TASK'` and a message naming the rejected value, return false, and send NOTHING — in particular do not fall back to the token-free frame, because the daemon would then approve a plan the human never reviewed. Build the outbound payload as a value typed against the APPROVE_TASK member of `PluginOutboundMessage` so the compiler binds the method to the wire type, and pass it through the existing `sendMessage`, preserving its boolean result verbatim so a disconnected or failed send still reports false. Under no circumstance read `this.state` / `currentState` in this method: the token is whatever the reviewed panel hands in, never the newest cached revision. Re-run the focused suite; groups A through G must pass.
implementationPlan.note:
approveTask is now `approveTask(taskId: string, expectedPlanRevision?: number): boolean` in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts.

Three branches, in this order:
1. `expectedPlanRevision === undefined` -> build `{ taskId }` and send. The key is genuinely never written, so JSON carries no trace of it. This is the entire backwards-compatibility contract for the four unchanged callers, and it is checked first so no validation can ever interfere with a legacy call.
2. Malformed supplied token -> log, fire onError with `operation: 'APPROVE_TASK'`, return false, send NOTHING. Explicitly no fallback to the token-free frame: that would hand the daemon an unchecked approval for a plan nobody reviewed, which is the hole this task exists to close.
3. Valid token -> `{ taskId, expectedPlanRevision }` through the same `sendMessage`, whose boolean is returned verbatim so a disconnected client or a throwing socket still reports false.

Validation is `typeof === 'number' && Number.isSafeInteger(v) && v >= 0`, no numeric conversion anywhere — `Number.isSafeInteger` alone covers fractional, NaN, Infinity and out-of-range, and a coercion would be the silent fallback the task forbids. The `typeof` guard is not redundant with the TS type: untyped webview messages reach this method (BoardViewProvider forwards `message.taskId` straight off a postMessage), so `null`/`'3'`/`true` are real runtime inputs, and `null` in particular passes the `!== undefined` gate.

Both payloads are typed `ApproveTaskPayload = Extract<PluginOutboundMessage, { type: 'APPROVE_TASK' }>['payload']`, a new local alias that reads the shape off the outbound union, so the compiler binds the method to the wire type instead of to a free-floating object literal. `PluginOutboundMessage` was added to the EXISTING `import type {...} from '../types/moe'` list — type-only, elided by ts.transpileModule, so no new runtime require appears and the peer strict-require-map tests are untouched.

The method does not reference `this.state` or `currentState` at all; the refusal message names the task, the rejected value and its typeof.

implementationPlan.description: GIVE THE PANEL CORRELATED REFUSAL FEEDBACK WITHOUT LEAKING CONTEXT. In moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts widen the `_onError` emitter payload type additively to `{ operation?: string; message: string; code?: number; codeName?: string; context?: { taskId?: string; expectedPlanRevision?: number; currentPlanRevision?: number } }`; existing subscribers read only operation and message and must keep compiling untouched. In the inbound ERROR case, keep the current message resolution as it is and fix the operation lookup to prefer the daemon's modern top-level field with the old nested one as fallback, so a stale-approval refusal is finally correlated to the command that caused it. Promote `code` only when it is a finite number and `codeName` only when it is a non-empty string, each with the same top-level-then-nested fallback. For context, write a small pure allowlist helper that copies at most `taskId` (string), `expectedPlanRevision` and `currentPlanRevision` (finite numbers) from the daemon context; never spread the received context object, because other daemon errors carry internal field names, reason strings and paths that must not reach the public event. Omit the context property entirely when none of the three survive. This is additive error handling only: an ERROR frame with none of the new fields must produce exactly the payload it produces today. Re-run the focused suite; groups H, I, J and K must pass.
implementationPlan.note:
Inbound ERROR handling in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts is now additively correlated, with a hard allowlist on context.

Type: `_onError` is `vscode.EventEmitter<DaemonErrorEvent>` where the new `DaemonErrorEvent` is `{ operation?, message, code?, codeName?, context?: DaemonErrorContext }` and `DaemonErrorContext` is `{ taskId?, expectedPlanRevision?, currentPlanRevision? }`. Everything past `message` is optional, so the widening is invisible to existing readers. Confirmed there are currently NO external onError subscribers anywhere under moe-vscode/src (grep returns only MoeDaemonClient's own lines), so nothing outside this file could break, and the compile proves it.

Lookup: `operation` is now `message.operation ?? payload?.operation`. Reading only the nested field was the pre-existing defect — the daemon emits operation at the TOP level (WebSocketServer.ts:1003), so operation was effectively always undefined and a stale-approval refusal arrived uncorrelated. Same top-level-then-nested fallback for `code` and `codeName`. The message resolution is untouched: `message.message ?? payload?.message ?? 'Unknown error'`, and the existing log line is unchanged.

Promotion is conditional, via spread of a short-circuit so a failed guard adds no key at all: `code` only when it is a number AND `Number.isFinite` (so the daemon's -32002 crosses but a string 'STATE_CONFLICT' does not), `codeName` only when it is a non-empty string.

Context: new module-level pure helper `allowlistedErrorContext(context: unknown)` next to `pathsMatch`. It rejects non-objects and null, then copies at most `taskId` (string), `expectedPlanRevision` and `currentPlanRevision` (finite numbers) into a fresh object, and returns `undefined` when nothing survives so the caller omits the property entirely instead of publishing `{}`. The received object is never spread — other daemon MoeErrors carry internal field names, reason strings and project paths, and `epicId` is emitted by the daemon too (it is listed in the inbound type precisely so its exclusion here is deliberate rather than accidental).

The ERROR case body needed braces to scope its three new consts; the rest of the switch already uses that style.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: (1) Typing the parameter `number | null` and treating null as legacy — rejected: the daemon treats an omitted key as the only legacy opt-out and refuses an explicit null, so mirroring that here keeps one rule across the wire. (2) Letting a malformed token fall back to the token-free frame so the human is not blocked — rejected outright: that is the exact hole this epic exists to close, since the daemon would then approve a plan nobody reviewed; refuse locally and report it. (3) Validating in the panel instead of the client — rejected: the panel slice is a separate card and every future caller would repeat the check; the client is the single wire boundary. (4) Spreading the daemon's error context straight into the public event — rejected: unrelated MoeErrors carry internal field names, reason strings and paths, so only three keys may cross. (5) Changing the four existing approval call sites to pass a token — explicitly out of scope and forbidden by a task rail; the optional parameter is what keeps them working untouched. (6) Writing the test against a hand-copied serializer — rejected: the existing metrics-view test executes production code through transpileModule plus vm, and that convention is what makes these assertions real.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: moe-vscode has no vitest; `npm test` is `node --test tests/*.test.cjs` and `npm run compile` is `tsc -p ./` over src only, so the new .cjs test is never type-checked but the compile still guards the callers. tests/metrics-view.test.cjs is the template: it reads the .ts source, transpiles it with the typescript devDependency and runs it in a vm context with stubbed requires. MoeDaemonClient imports vscode, fs, path, net, child_process and ws, so all six need stubs; the constructor takes only an extensionPath, and the socket plus connection state are private fields a test can inject through bracket access. `sendMessage(type, payload)` already returns boolean and, on a throwing send, logs, fires the error event, tears down the half-dead socket and returns false — preserve that result verbatim rather than re-implementing it. `approveTask` is at line 388 and simply delegates. The ERROR case near line 971 currently reads `payload?.operation` only, while the daemon sends `operation` at the TOP level, so operation is effectively always undefined today; that is the pre-existing defect this slice fixes additively. TASK_UPDATED at line 775 replaces the entire cached task object, so planRevision flows through the state path for free once the type carries it — no update logic to write, only a regression test. The `DaemonInboundMessage` ERROR member is the minimal `{ type: 'ERROR'; message: string }` and needs widening before the new fields can be read type-safely.
planningNotes.risks: A falsy check such as `if (expectedPlanRevision)` silently drops revision 0, which is precisely the legacy-row value — the zero test exists to kill that mutant. Any numeric conversion of the supplied token reintroduces the coercion this task forbids; `Number.isSafeInteger` plus a non-negative check is the whole rule. Asserting an omitted key with an undefined comparison passes even when the property is serialized, so assert key absence and compare the parsed frame. JSON.stringify drops an undefined-valued property, which makes a sloppy implementation look correct in the wire test while still being wrong in typed code — build the payload without the key instead of assigning undefined. The client must never consult cached state for a token; a test with a differing cached revision guards that rail. Widening the error event payload is only safe while every field stays optional, since existing subscribers destructure operation and message. Do not promote epicId or any other daemon context key, and do not report success on a disconnected send. JetBrains ships first by epic rail, and the reviewed-versus-latest binding lives in the following webview slice, so do not claim this slice makes the sent revision provably the rendered one.

No numeric conversion anywhere — coercion is the silent fallback this task exists to prevent. A malformed token (null, '3', true, 3.5, -1, MAX_SAFE_INTEGER+1, NaN, Infinity — all eight tested) logs, fires onError with operation APPROVE_TASK and a message naming the value and its typeof, returns false, and sends NOTHING AT ALL. The `typeof` guard is live, not dead code — untyped webview postMessage fields reach this method. `sendMessage`'s boolean is returned verbatim, so disconnected, no-socket and throwing-socket all report false with no false success.

ERROR PROMOTION: onError's payload is widened additively to { operation?, message, code?, codeName?, context? }; there are currently no external onError subscribers
